Octo (UC Berkeley, 2024)\\n\\n| 字段 | 信息 |\\n|------|------|\\n| 参数量 | 27M (Small) / 93M (Base) |\\n| Vision encoder | Shallow CNN (从头训练，非预训练 ViT) |\\n| **Connector 类型** | **CNN patch encoder → 直接拼接进 transformer（无独立 connector）** |\\n| LLM backbone | 纯 transformer（非预训练 LLM），decoder-only |\\n| 开源状态 | ✅ weights + code, GitHub: [octo-models/octo](https://github.com/octo-models/octo), HF: rail-berkeley/octo-base |\\n| LIBERO 支持 | ✅ 原生支持，fine-tune 后 ~72% SR |\\n| 改造成本 | 低（已有 LIBERO fine-tune 代码） |\\n| 论文 LIBERO 结果 | 有: ~72% (fine-tuned) |\\n| 备注 | 非标准 VLM→LLM 架构，是 transformer-based diffusion policy。图像通过浅层 CNN 编码为 16×16 patches 后直接拼入 transformer 序列。语言用 T5 tokenizer/encoder。Action head 是 diffusion policy。 |\\n\\n### 2. CogACT (Microsoft/Tsinghua, 2024)\\n\\n| 字段 | 信息 |\\n|------|------|\\n| 参数量 | ~7.1B (7B Prismatic VLM + 89M-300M DiT action module) |\\n| Vision encoder | DINOv2 + SigLIP (双 encoder，channel 拼接) |\\n| **Connector 类型** | **2-layer MLP projector**（Prismatic 架构：DINOv2+SigLIP feature → channel concat → 2-layer MLP → Llama-2 embedding space） |\\n| LLM backbone | Llama-2 7B (via Prismatic-7B) |\\n| 开源状态 | ✅ weights + code, GitHub: [microsoft/CogACT](https://github.com/microsoft/CogACT), HF: CogACT/CogACT-Base, CogACT/CogACT-Small |\\n| LIBERO 支持 | 需改造（paper 用 SimplerEnv + 真机） |\\n| 改造成本 | 中（需接 LIBERO data pipeline + action space） |\\n| 论文 LIBERO 结果 | 无 |\\n| 备注 | 核心创新在 DiT action module（将 VLM 认知特征作为 condition 输入扩散 transformer 生成动作）。Connector 与 OpenVLA 相同（都基于 Prismatic） |\\n\\n### 3. RT-2-X (Google DeepMind, 2023)\\n\\n| 字段 | 信息 |\\n|------|------|\\n| 参数量 | 55B |\\n| Vision encoder | ViT (PaLI-X 的视觉编码器) |\\n| **Connector 类型** | 未公开（闭源） |\\n| LLM backbone | PaLI-X / PaLM-E |\\n| 开源状态 | ❌ **闭源**，权重不公开 |\\n| LIBERO 支持 | 不可行 |\\n| 改造成本 | 不可行 |\\n| 论文 LIBERO 结果 | 无 |\\n| 备注 | 闭源模型，无法使用 |\\n\\n### 5. GR-1 (ByteDance, 2023)\\n\\n| 字段 | 信息 |\\n|------|------|\\n| 参数量 | 未明确公布 |\\n| Vision encoder | MAE ViT-Base (预训练) |\\n| **Connector 类型** | **Perceiver Resampler**（将 MAE ViT 视觉 token 数量压缩）+ linear layers 对齐维度 |\\n| LLM backbone | GPT-style causal transformer（非预训练 LLM） |\\n| 开源状态 | ✅ weights + code, GitHub: [bytedance/GR-1](https://github.com/bytedance/GR-1), Apache-2.0 |\\n| LIBERO 支持 | 需改造（paper 只有 CALVIN） |\\n| 改造成本 | 高（需改 data pipeline、action space、视频生成部分可能要适配） |\\n| 论文 LIBERO 结果 | 无（CALVIN: 94.9%） |\\n| 备注 | 既做动作预测又做视频生成（future image prediction）。语言用 CLIP text encoder。使用 Perceiver Resampler 这一点很有价值——与 RoboFlamingo 类似但架构不同。 |\\n\\n### 6. RoboVLMs (2024)\\n\\n| 字段 | 信息 |\\n|------|------|\\n| 参数量 | 不定（框架） |\\n| Vision encoder | 支持多种 VLM backbone |\\n| **Connector 类型** | 取决于所选 VLM（框架支持多种） |\\n| LLM backbone | 取决于所选 VLM |\\n| 开源状态 | ✅ code + models, GitHub: [Robot-VLAs/RoboVLMs](https://github.com/Robot-VLAs/RoboVLMs) |\\n| LIBERO 支持 | 需确认 |\\n| 改造成本 | 低-中（框架设计灵活） |\\n| 论文 LIBERO 结果 | 未确认 |\\n| 备注 | 这是一个**框架**而非单一模型。实验了 8+ VLM backbone × 4 policy 架构。最佳模型用 Kosmos backbone。对我们的 connector 对比研究有参考价值但不直接使用。 |\\n\\n### 9. 3D-VLA (UMass, ICML 2024)\\n\\n| 字段 | 信息 |\\n|------|------|\\n| 参数量 | 未明确 |\\n| Vision encoder | 3D feature extraction（point cloud based） |\\n| **Connector 类型** | **Interaction tokens**（3D-LLM 架构，用交互 token 嵌入 embodied 环境） |\\n| LLM backbone | 基于 3D-LLM |\\n| 开源状态 | ✅ code + diffusion models, GitHub: [UMass-Embodied-AGI/3D-VLA](https://github.com/UMass-Embodied-AGI/3D-VLA), HF: anyezhy |\\n| LIBERO 支持 | 需大量改造（paper 用 RLBench） |\\n| 改造成本 | 高（3D 点云输入，与 LIBERO 2D 图像差异大） |\\n| 论文 LIBERO 结果 | 无 |\\n| 备注 | 基于 3D 点云的 VLA，与我们研究的 2D 图像 → connector → LLM 管道差异太大，不推荐 |\\n\\n### 10. π0 / pi-zero (Physical Intelligence, 2024-2025)\\n\\n| 字段 | 信息 |\\n|------|------|\\n| 参数量 | ~3.3B (400M SigLIP + 2.6B Gemma + ~300M action expert) |\\n| Vision encoder | SigLIP-So400m (400M params) |\\n| **Connector 类型** | **Linear projection**（单层线性层，将 SigLIP token 投影到 Gemma embedding space） |\\n| LLM backbone | Gemma 2B (via PaliGemma) |\\n| 开源状态 | ✅ weights + code, GitHub: [Physical-Intelligence/openpi](https://github.com/Physical-Intelligence/openpi), HF 有 PyTorch port |\\n| LIBERO 支持 | ✅ 有评测（LIBERO-PRO 中被评测） |\\n| 改造成本 | 低（已有 LIBERO 评测代码） |\\n| 论文 LIBERO 结果 | 有（LIBERO-PRO 中有结果） |\\n| 备注 | **强力推荐**。Linear projection 是最简单的 connector，与 OpenVLA 的 2-layer MLP 形成鲜明对比。Action expert 通过 MoE 架构耦合。Flow matching 生成动作。 |\\n\\n### 11. OpenVLA-OFT (Stanford, 2025)\\n\\n| 字段 | 信息 |\\n|------|------|\\n| 参数量 | 7B |\\n| Vision encoder | SigLIP + DINOv2 (Prismatic) |\\n| **Connector 类型** | **2-layer MLP projector**（与 OpenVLA 相同的 Prismatic connector） |\\n| LLM backbone | Llama-2 7B |\\n| 开源状态 | ✅ weights + code, GitHub: [moojink/openvla-oft](https://github.com/moojink/openvla-oft) |\\n| LIBERO 支持 | ✅ 原生支持，SOTA 97.1% |\\n| 改造成本 | 极低（已有完整 LIBERO fine-tune + eval） |\\n| 论文 LIBERO 结果 | 有: 97.1% SR (4 suite avg) |\\n| 备注 | Connector 与 OpenVLA 完全相同。改进在 fine-tuning recipe（continuous actions, action chunking, bidirectional attention）。对压缩实验来说，connector 级别的差异与 OpenVLA 相同，但 action generation 方式不同，可能影响压缩行为。 |\\n\\n### 12. |---------------|----------|------|--------|
| **Linear projection** | **π0**, X-VLA, SpatialVLA | 最简单的 connector，单层线性变换 | ⭐⭐⭐ 高 |
| **Cross-attention (Flamingo-style)** | **RoboMM** | 不在 encoder 端压缩，而是 decoder 端通过 cross-attention 选择性融合 | ⭐⭐ 中 |
| **CNN patch → direct concat** | Octo | 无独立 connector，图像 patches 直接拼入 transformer | ⭐ 低（架构差异太大） |
| **MLP merger + spatial grouping** | LingBot-VLA | 先空间合并再 MLP 投射 + cross-attention | ⭐⭐ 中 |
| **Cross-attention tokenizer** | HPT | learnable tokens 通过 cross-attention 聚合 vision features | ⭐ 低（非 VLM 架构） |

### 关键发现
1. **Linear projection** 是最有价值的新增类型——π0 和 X-VLA 都用这种最简单的 connector，与 OpenVLA 的 2-layer MLP 形成对比
2. **Cross-attention** (RoboMM 的 OpenFlamingo 架构) 从根本上不同：不投射拼接，而是 decoder 层间交叉注意力
3. 大量模型共享 connector：OpenVLA, CogACT, LLARVA, TraceVLA, ECoT, OpenVLA-OFT 都用 **2-layer MLP**（Prismatic 或 LLaVA 架构）

---

## Top 推荐：最适合扩展实验的 5 个模型

### 🥇 1. π0 (Physical Intelligence)
- **Connector**: Linear projection (单层线性)
- **推荐理由**: 
  - 与 OpenVLA 的 2-layer MLP 形成直接对比（linear vs MLP）
  - 开源权重 + 代码，社区活跃
  - 已有 LIBERO 评测代码
  - PaliGemma 架构广为人知
  - 3B 参数可在单卡运行
- **预期价值**: Linear projection 不增加非线性变换，token 可能保留更多原始 visual feature 结构 → 压缩行为可能与 MLP 不同

### 🥈 2. X-VLA
- **Connector**: Linear projection + soft prompts
- **推荐理由**:
  - 同样是 linear projection，与 π0 对比看 soft prompt 的影响
  - LIBERO 98% SR，已有训练好的 LIBERO 权重直接可用
  - 0.9B 参数，实验成本最低
  - ICLR 2026，最新模型
  - Apache-2.0 开源
- **预期价值**: 验证 linear projection 的压缩行为是否 consistent across models

### 🥉 3. DeeR-VLA
- **Connector**: Perceiver Resampler + Cross-attention (OpenFlamingo)
- **推荐理由**:
  - Perceiver Resampler 与 RoboFlamingo 相同架构，但 DeeR-VLA 已验证可训练（CALVIN benchmark 正常工作）
  - 给 Perceiver Resampler 第二次机会
  - 可对比 RoboFlamingo 的训练失败是架构问题还是实现问题
  - Open source with checkpoints
- **预期价值**: Perceiver Resampler 本身就做了 attention-based compression → 压缩行为可能与 MLP/linear 截然不同
- **风险**: LIBERO 需要自己改造

### 4. RoboMM
- **Connector**: Cross-attention (OpenFlamingo) + 3D Adapter
- **推荐理由**:
  - Cross-attention 融合方式从根本上不同于 projection-based connectors
  - 已有 LIBERO 结果 (90.7%)
  - Open source
- **预期价值**: Cross-attention 在 decoder 端动态选择 visual features → 可能展现出与 projection-based 完全不同的压缩模式
- **风险**: 架构较复杂，3D adapter 增加变量

### 5. OpenVLA-OFT
- **Connector**: 2-layer MLP projector (与 OpenVLA 相同)
- **推荐理由**:
  - Connector 与 OpenVLA 相同，但 action generation 完全不同（continuous + chunking）
  - LIBERO 97.1% SOTA
  - 可验证 "相同 connector + 不同 action head" 是否影响压缩行为
  - 已有完整 LIBERO 代码
- **预期价值**: 作为 OpenVLA 的对照组，隔离 connector vs action head 对压缩的影响

---

## 不推荐的模型及原因

| 模型 | 排除原因 |
|------|----------|
| RT-2-X | 闭源，权重不可用 |
| GR-2 | 未开源 |
| 3D-VLA | 3D 点云输入，与 2D VLA 差异太大 |
| CogACT | Connector 与 OpenVLA 相同（Prismatic MLP），不新增类型 |
| LLARVA | Connector 与 OpenVLA 类似（MLP projector），不新增类型 |
| TraceVLA | Connector 与 OpenVLA 相同，不新增类型 |
| ECoT | Connector 与 OpenVLA 相同，不新增类型 |
| HPT | 非 VLM 架构，不适合 connector 压缩叙事 |
| GR-1 | 有 Perceiver Resampler（有价值），但无 LIBERO 支持 + 视频生成架构改造成本高 |
| Octo | 无独立 connector（CNN patch 直接拼入），架构与标准 VLM 差异太大 |

---

## 总结：Connector 类型 × 模型矩阵

| Connector 类型 | 已有 | 推荐新增 |
|---------------|------|----------|
| Pixel-shuffle | SmolVLA ✅ | — |
| 2-layer MLP projector | OpenVLA ✅ | OpenVLA-OFT（同 connector 不同 action head） |
| Perceiver Resampler | RoboFlamingo ❌(失败) | **DeeR-VLA** |
| **Linear projection** | — | **π0, X-VLA** |
| **Cross-attention** | — | **RoboMM** |

实现后可达 **5 种 connector 类型 × 6+ 模型**的全面对比。

## X-VLA Overview

X-VLA has been accepted to ICLR 2026, and won 1st Place (Champion) at the AgiBot World Challenge, held at IROS 2025.

## What is X-VLA?

X-VLA is a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model that introduces a soft prompt mechanism — embodiment-specific learnable embeddings that guide a unified Transformer backbone toward effective multi-domain policy learning. The X-VLA-0.9B model achieves state-of-the-art generalization across six simulation platforms and three real-world robots, surpassing prior VLA approaches in dexterity, adaptability, and efficiency.

## GitHub Repository

The official GitHub repository is available at: **https://github.com/2toinf/X-VLA**

X-VLA is now natively integrated into the LeRobot platform, and the code is open source under the Apache License 2.0.

## Key Features

X-VLA adopts a Server–Client architecture to separate the model environment from simulation or robot-specific dependencies, which avoids package conflicts and supports distributed inference across GPUs, SLURM clusters, or edge devices.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the X-VLA robot vision language action model:

## Overview
X-VLA-0.9B achieves state-of-the-art generalization across six simulation platforms and three real-world robots, surpassing prior VLA approaches in dexterity, adaptability, and efficiency.

## Architecture and Training
The X-VLA 0.9B parameter model was trained with a carefully designed data processing and learning recipe, with the training pipeline pretrained on 290K episodes from Droid, Robomind, and Agibot, spanning seven platforms across five types of robotic arms. By leveraging soft prompts to absorb embodiment-specific variations, the model learns an embodiment-agnostic generalist policy.

## LIBERO Performance
The model attains over 90% success rates on several benchmarks, including Libero at 98%. By tuning only 1% of the model parameters (9M), X-VLA-0.9B achieves 93% success rate on LIBERO and 54% on Simpler-WidowX.

## Key Innovation: Soft Prompts
A new set of soft prompts is introduced and optimized to encode the hardware configuration of a novel domain, while the pretrained backbone remains frozen. Soft Prompts offer a simple, scalable mechanism for unifying diverse robotic data, paving the way toward adaptable, cross-embodiment robot foundation models.

## Code Structure and Model Architecture

All models share a consistent architecture: configuration_xvla.py, modeling_xvla.py, and unified tokenizer (tokenizer.json). X-VLA adopts a Server–Client architecture to separate the model environment from simulation or robot-specific dependencies.

## Core Model Design

X-VLA introduces a soft prompt mechanism — embodiment-specific learnable embeddings that guide a unified Transformer backbone toward effective multi-domain policy learning. The resulting architecture — X-VLA-0.9B — achieves state-of-the-art generalization across six simulation platforms and three real-world robots, surpassing prior VLA approaches in dexterity, adaptability, and efficiency.

## Florence Encoder Integration

The codebase references Florence2 for multimodal fusion capabilities. The implementation includes handling of Florence2 configuration that must provide `projection_dim` for multimodal fusion.

## Model Variants

The X-VLA-Pt model is the foundation checkpoint, trained across multiple robot domains. Each embodiment is fine-tuned for its respective environment while retaining cross-embodiment alignment.

The project is an ICLR 2026 submission implementing "Soft-Prompted Transformer as Scalable Cross-Embodiment Vision-Language-Action Model."

X-VLA-Libero is a model fine-tuned on the LIBERO benchmark running on a Franka robot, achieving 98.1% on LIBERO Eval.

The X-VLA repository contains several key components: all models share a consistent architecture including configuration_xvla.py, modeling_xvla.py, and unified tokenizer (tokenizer.json).

Regarding the soft prompt approach, X-VLA is a flow-matching-based VLA architecture that relies exclusively on soft-prompted standard Transformer encoders, enjoying both scalability and simplicity. Additionally, the model supports Parameter efficient finetuning (PEFT) techniques for fast adaptation.

The repository includes evaluation guidance for multiple benchmarks, and to evaluate across different simulations, users need to set up the corresponding environments including Libero, Simpler, Calvin, VLABench, and NAVSIM.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about the X-VLA architecture (arxiv 2510.10274):

## X-VLA Architecture Overview

X-VLA is a flow-matching-based VLA architecture that relies exclusively on soft-prompted standard Transformer encoders.

## Vision Encoder Components

The architecture adopts Florence-Large as the vision-language encoder and employs a standard Transformer backbone with 24 layers and a hidden size of 1024 for action generation.

A pretrained VLM encoder (Florence-Large) is used for the main vision-language stream (fixed-view and instruction), while auxiliary views such as wrist-views are processed with a shared vision backbone.

## Core Approach

The model proposes a novel Soft Prompt approach with minimally added parameters, by infusing prompt learning concepts into cross-embodiment robot learning and introducing separate sets of learnable embeddings for each distinct data source.

Note: While your query mentioned DaViT and 577 vision tokens, the search results indicate that DaViT is used in Florence-2 (a different model), and Florence-Large is the primary vision encoder used in X-VLA. You may want to check the full PDF of the paper for specific details about vision token counts and additional architectural specifications.

# X-VLA Architecture Details

## 1. Vision Encoder
**Model:** Florence-Large (Xiao et al., 2024)
- Processes main fixed-view images and language instructions together
- Auxiliary views (wrist-camera) use a "shared vision backbone" separately
- Exact token count and resolution not specified in the document

## 2. Connector/Projection
The document states the architecture includes "dedicated encoding strategies to align" modalities, but specific connector dimensions are not disclosed. Only that there are "domain-specific output projections" for actions.

## 3. LLM Backbone
**Transformer configuration:**
- 24 transformer layers
- Hidden size: 1024
- "Standard Transformer encoders" for multimodal feature fusion
- "Simple stacking" of self-attention blocks

## 4. Soft Prompts
- Learnable embeddings denoted as P^H = {p_i} for each data source
- "Injected into the model at the early stage of action generation"
- Dimension k not explicitly stated
- Account for only 0.04% of total parameters

## 5. Action Head
**Flow-matching approach:**
- Generates 30 anchor points over 4-second horizon (through temporal downsampling)
- EEF representation: xyz position + Rotate6D rotation + binary gripper state
- Loss functions: MSE for position/rotation, BCE for gripper

## 6. Parameter Breakdown
- **Total:** 0.9B parameters (X-VLA-0.9B instantiation)
- Soft prompts + action projections: "small fraction (0.04%)"
- Vision-language modules: frozen or reduced learning rate
- No detailed per-component breakdown provided

# X-VLA Repository Summary

## 1. Repository Structure

Main directories include:
- **datasets/** — data handling and domain configurations
- **evaluation/** — benchmark-specific evaluation scripts (LIBERO, Calvin, Google Robot, etc.)
- **models/** — core model architecture files

Key files: `train.py`, `peft_train.py`, `deploy.py`, `requirements.txt`, `environment.yml`

## 2. Installation & Environment Setup

The repository provides two installation methods:

```
conda create -n XVLA python=3.10 -y
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

Or using Conda environment file:
```
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate xvla-stable
```

## 3. LIBERO Evaluation

For LIBERO benchmarking, use the fine-tuned checkpoint `2toINF/X-VLA-Libero`. The documentation states: "For questions about converting relative actions to absolute actions..." refer to GitHub issues #2 and #15, with "full preprocessing guidance" available in `evaluation/libero/preprocess.md`. Performance achieves **98.1%** success rate.

LoRA adapter variants are also available (`X-VLA-libero-spatial-peft`, `X-VLA-libero-object-peft`, etc.).

## 4. Model Loading Code

```python
from transformers import AutoModel, AutoProcessor
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained("2toINF/X-VLA-WidowX", 
                                   trust_remote_code=True)
processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained("2toINF/X-VLA-WidowX", 
                                          trust_remote_code=True)
```

## 5. Vision Tokens, Projection, Connector

The documentation does **not** contain explicit mentions of vision token counts, projection layers, or connector specifications.

## 6. Server-Client Architecture

The system employs a "Server–Client architecture to separate the model environment from simulation or robot-specific dependencies." The server launches via:

```python
model.run(processor, host="0.0.0.0", port=8000)
```

Clients send POST requests to `http://<server_ip>:8000/act` with JSON payloads containing proprioceptive state, language instructions, images, domain ID, and denoising steps. Each domain has reference client implementations under `evaluation/<domain>/<robot>/client.py`.

# Code Analysis: X-VLA Vision-Language-Action Model

## 1. Vision Encoder Initialization

The model uses **Florence2** as the vision backbone:

```python
self.vlm = Florence2ForConditionalGeneration(config.florence_config).to(torch.float32)
```

The encoder processes multi-view images through `self.vlm._encode_image(valid_images)`, returning shape `[#valid, N, D]` where N is the number of image tokens and D is the projection dimension.

## 2. Projection/Connector Layer

The projection dimension is extracted from Florence2's config:

```python
projection_dim = getattr(self.vlm.config, "projection_dim", None)
if projection_dim is None:
    raise ValueError("Florence2 config must provide `projection_dim`...")
```

No explicit nn.Linear projection layer is shown in this file. The `projection_dim` parameter is passed to the transformer as `multi_modal_input_size`.

## 3. Vision-Action Token Sequencing

The code shows:
- **Primary view** (image 0): merged with language embeddings via `_merge_input_ids_with_image_features()`
- **Auxiliary views** (remaining images): flattened separately as `aux_visual_inputs`

```python
merged_embeds, attention_mask = self.vlm._merge_input_ids_with_image_features(
    image_features[:, 0], # first view
    inputs_embeds, # language
)
```

Soft prompts and action tokens are handled by `SoftPromptedTransformer`.

## 4. Forward Method Signature (Training)

```python
def forward(self, input_ids: torch.LongTensor, image_input: torch.FloatTensor,
            image_mask: torch.Tensor, domain_id: torch.LongTensor, 
            proprio: torch.Tensor, action: torch.Tensor) -> Dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
```

**Flow**: 
1. Encode multimodal inputs via `forward_vlm()`
2. Apply diffusion-style noising to actions
3. Preprocess via action_space
4. Transformer prediction
5. Compute loss

## 5. Vision-Related Keywords in Class

Now I have a comprehensive picture. Let me also check what the Florence-2 vision encoder actually produces in terms of token count. Let me look at the code more carefully.

Actually, I recall from the Florence-2 paper and code that:
- Florence-2-large uses DaViT-Large as vision encoder
- For 224×224 input, DaViT-Large produces features at the last stage of 7×7 = 49 spatial locations
- But Florence-2 also has a multi-scale image projection that can produce more tokens

In the Florence-2 HuggingFace implementation, the `_encode_image` method:


1. Passes the image through DaViT → gets features from the last stage
2. Applies the image_projection which includes adaptive average pooling and linear projection
3. The output depends on the config settings

The `image_feature_source: ["spatial_avg_pool", "temporal_avg_pool"]` suggests spatial pooling reduces features to a single token while temporal pooling is for video. Looking at the actual implementation, `_encode_image` returns features shaped as `[B, num_tokens, projection_dim]`, but I need to trace through exactly how many tokens that actually produces.

For Florence-2-large processing 224×224 images, the DaViT backbone outputs 7×7 spatial features, which the projection layer maps to 1024-dimensional tokens—so roughly 49 tokens per image. In X-VLA's setup with three views, that's potentially 147 vision tokens total, though the primary view gets special treatment through the VLM encoder with language merging while the auxiliary views are handled separately. Now I'm trying to understand how the VTC component fits into this pipeline.

VTC should slot in right after Florence-2 encodes the image features but before the merge step, compressing those ~49 tokens per view down to something smaller. It's a relatively modest compression target compared to OpenVLA's 256 tokens, so VTC could reduce 49 tokens to 24, 12, or even 6 depending on the compression ratio we want. This actually creates an interesting angle for the paper—showing how linear projection models behave under compression even when starting with a smaller token count than typical vision transformers.

For the actual implementation in X-VLA, I need to hook into the Florence2ForConditionalGeneration backbone right after the `_encode_image()` call returns the vision features as a [B, N, D] tensor, apply VTC to compress it down to [B, K, D] where K is smaller than N, then continue with the rest of the pipeline.

The tricky part is that Florence2's merge function expects a specific number of vision tokens to match the `<image>` placeholders in the text input, so I'd need to modify that merge step too. Another option is inserting VTC inside the SoftPromptedTransformer after the VLM outputs but before the transformer layers process them—that might be cleaner since the features are already merged at that point. Let me check the Florence2 source to confirm the exact token counts, then look at how our existing VTC implementation integrates with other models so I can write this up properly.

"""Smart Compress Training: VisionTokenCompressor + OpenVLA on LIBERO.

Usage:
    python train_openvla_smart_compress.py --config configs/openvla_smart_compress_m32.yaml
    python train_openvla_smart_compress.py --config configs/openvla_smart_compress_m32.yaml --dry-run
    python train_openvla_smart_compress.py --config configs/openvla_smart_compress_m32.yaml --resume checkpoints/openvla_sc_m32/latest

Trainable: VisionTokenCompressor only.
Frozen: DINOv2 + SigLIP + projector + Llama-2 7B.

OpenVLA uses autoregressive action prediction: continuous actions are discretized
to 256-bin tokens, and the LLM generates them via cross-entropy loss.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import faulthandler
faulthandler.enable()
import argparse
import copy
import json
import logging
import os
import signal
import sys
import time as time_module
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional

import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F
import yaml

logging.basicConfig(
    level=logging.INFO,
    format="%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s",
    datefmt="%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S",
)
log = logging.getLogger(__name__)

ARTIFACTS_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
sys.path.insert(0, str(ARTIFACTS_DIR))

from openvla_vtc_adapter import (
    OpenVLAActionTokenizer,
    OpenVLASmartCompressWrapper,
    VisionTokenCompressor,
)


# ---- config loading ----

def load_config(config_path: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    config_path = Path(config_path)
    with open(config_path) as f:
        config = yaml.safe_load(f)
    if "_base_" in config:
        base_path = config_path.parent / config.pop("_base_")
        base_config = load_config(str(base_path))
        base_config = deep_merge(base_config, config)
        return base_config
    return config


def deep_merge(base: Dict, override: Dict) -> Dict:
    result = copy.deepcopy(base)
    for k, v in override.items():
        if k in result and isinstance(result[k], dict) and isinstance(v, dict):
            result[k] = deep_merge(result[k], v)
        else:
            result[k] = copy.deepcopy(v)
    return result


def set_seed(seed: int):
    import random
    random.seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)


# ---- model loading ----

def load_openvla_model(config: Dict[str, Any], device: torch.device):
    """Load OpenVLA model and processor from HuggingFace."""
    from transformers import AutoModelForVision2Seq, AutoProcessor

    model_cfg = config["model"]
    pretrained = model_cfg.get("pretrained", "openvla/openvla-7b")
    dtype_str = model_cfg.get("dtype", "float32")
    dtype_map = {"float32": torch.float32, "bfloat16": torch.bfloat16, "float16": torch.float16}
    torch_dtype = dtype_map.get(dtype_str, torch.float32)

    log.info("Loading OpenVLA from %s (dtype=%s)", pretrained, dtype_str)

    model = AutoModelForVision2Seq.from_pretrained(
        pretrained,
        torch_dtype=torch_dtype,
        trust_remote_code=True,
        low_cpu_mem_usage=True,
    )
    processor = AutoProcessor.from_pretrained(
        pretrained,
        trust_remote_code=True,
    )

    model.to(device)
    log.info("OpenVLA loaded: %d params", sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()))
    return model, processor


def wrap_with_compressor(
    model, processor, config: Dict[str, Any]
) -> OpenVLASmartCompressWrapper:
    """Create SmartCompressWrapper around OpenVLA."""
    compress_cfg = config.get("compressor", {})
    wrapper = OpenVLASmartCompressWrapper(
        model, processor, compress_config=compress_cfg
    )
    return wrapper


def freeze_for_compress_training(wrapper: OpenVLASmartCompressWrapper, config=None):
    """Freeze all OpenVLA parameters. Trainable: VTC compressor + LoRA (if enabled)."""
    for param in wrapper.model.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = False

    for param in wrapper.compressor.parameters():
        param.requires_grad = True

    if config and config.get("lora", {}).get("enabled", False):
        for name, param in wrapper.model.named_parameters():
            if "lora_" in name:
                param.requires_grad = True

    trainable = sum(p.numel() for p in wrapper.parameters() if p.requires_grad)
    total = sum(p.numel() for p in wrapper.parameters())
    comp_params = sum(p.numel() for p in wrapper.compressor.parameters())
    lora_params = sum(
        p.numel() for n, p in wrapper.model.named_parameters()
        if p.requires_grad and "lora_" in n
    )
    log.info(
        "Freeze config: trainable=%d / total=%d (%.4f%%)",
        trainable, total, 100 * trainable / total,
    )
    log.info("  Compressor params: %d", comp_params)

"""OpenVLA VTC Adapter: Vision Token Compressor for OpenVLA (Prismatic + Llama-2 7B).

Compresses N projected vision tokens to M tokens using learnable cross-attention,
then runs standard autoregressive generation through the frozen LLM.

Architecture:
  DINOv2+SigLIP (frozen) -> MLP projector (frozen) -> N tokens x 4096
  -> VisionTokenCompressor (trainable) -> M tokens x 4096
  -> Llama-2 7B (frozen) -> action token logits -> cross-entropy loss

Differences from SmolVLA VTC (smart_compress_module.py):
  - hidden_dim: 960 -> 4096 (Llama-2 7B)
  - Vision tokens per camera: 128 -> 256 (DINOv2+SigLIP fused per-patch)
  - Action paradigm: flow matching -> autoregressive (256-bin discretized tokens)
  - No separate action expert; standard LM head generates action tokens

Dependencies: torch, transformers (OpenVLA loaded via trust_remote_code=True)
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import math
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Tuple, Union

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F
from torch import Tensor


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# VisionTokenCompressor (self-contained, same architecture as SmolVLA version)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class CrossAttentionBlock(nn.Module):
    """Pre-norm cross-attention + FFN block."""

    def __init__(self, hidden_dim: int, num_heads: int, dropout: float = 0.1):
        super().__init__()
        self.norm_q = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim)
        self.norm_kv = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim)
        self.cross_attn = nn.MultiheadAttention(
            embed_dim=hidden_dim,
            num_heads=num_heads,
            dropout=dropout,
            batch_first=True,
        )
        self.norm_ffn = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim)
        self.ffn = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim, hidden_dim * 4),
            nn.GELU(),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
            nn.Linear(hidden_dim * 4, hidden_dim),
            nn.Dropout(dropout),
        )

    def forward(self, queries: Tensor, kv: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        q = self.norm_q(queries)
        kv_n = self.norm_kv(kv)
        attn_out, _ = self.cross_attn(q, kv_n, kv_n)
        queries = queries + attn_out
        queries = queries + self.ffn(self.norm_ffn(queries))
        return queries


class VisionTokenCompressor(nn.Module):
    """Cross-attention pooling: compress N vision tokens to M tokens.

    Args:
        hidden_dim: dimension of projected vision tokens (4096 for Llama-2 7B).
        num_queries: M, number of compressed output tokens.
        num_heads: attention heads per cross-attention layer.
        num_layers: number of cross-attention + FFN blocks.
        dropout: dropout rate.
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        hidden_dim: int = 4096,
        num_queries: int = 32,
        num_heads: int = 16,
        num_layers: int = 2,
        dropout: float = 0.1,
    ):
        super().__init__()
        self.num_queries = num_queries
        self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim

        self.queries = nn.Parameter(torch.randn(1, num_queries, hidden_dim) * 0.02)

        self.layers = nn.ModuleList(
            [CrossAttentionBlock(hidden_dim, num_heads, dropout) for _ in range(num_layers)]
        )
        self.output_norm = nn.LayerNorm(hidden_dim)

    def forward(self, vision_tokens: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        """
        Args:
            vision_tokens: (B, N, D) projected vision tokens (possibly from multiple cameras).
        Returns:
            (B, M, D) compressed tokens.
        """
        B = vision_tokens.shape[0]
        queries = self.queries.expand(B, -1, -1)
        for layer in self.layers:
            queries = layer(queries, vision_tokens)
        return self.output_norm(queries)


# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Action Tokenizer
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------


class OpenVLAActionTokenizer:
    """Discretize continuous actions to/from OpenVLA action token IDs.

    OpenVLA adds 256 special action tokens to the vocabulary. Each continuous
    action dimension is independently discretized into one of 256 bins.

    Args:
        tokenizer: HuggingFace tokenizer from OpenVLA processor.
        n_bins: number of discretization bins (default 256).
        min_action: per-dim minimum for normalization, shape (action_dim,).
        max_action: per-dim maximum for normalization, shape (action_dim,).
    """

    def __init__(
        self,
        tokenizer,
        n_bins: int = 256,
        min_action: Optional[Tensor] = None,
        max_action: Optional[Tensor] = None,
    ):
        self.tokenizer = tokenizer
        self.n_bins = n_bins
        self.min_action = min_action
        self.max_action = max_action
        self.action_token_begin_id = self._find_action_token_begin(tokenizer)

    @staticmethod
    def _find_action_token_begin(tokenizer) -> int:
        """Find the first action token ID in the vocabulary."""
        vocab = tokenizer.get_vocab()
        # OpenVLA convention: tokens named like "v0_token_0" .. "v0_token_255"
        # or "ACTION_0" .. "ACTION_255" depending on version
        candidates = []
        for token, idx in vocab.items():
            for pattern in ("v0_token_", "ACTION_", "action_"):
                if token.startswith(pattern):
                    try:
                        bin_id = int(token[len(pattern):])
                        candidates.append((bin_id, idx))
                    except ValueError:
                        continue
        if candidates:
            candidates.sort(key=lambda x: x[0])
            return candidates[0][1]
        # Fallback: assume last n_bins tokens are action tokens
        return len(tokenizer) - 256

    def encode(self, actions: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        """Discretize continuous actions to token IDs.

        Args:
            actions: (..., action_dim) continuous actions.
        Returns:
            (..., action_dim) token IDs (long).
        """
        if self.min_action is not None and self.max_action is not None:
            lo = self.min_action.to(actions.device)
            hi = self.max_action.to(actions.device)
            normalized = (actions - lo) / (hi - lo + 1e-8)
        else:
            normalized = (actions + 1.0) / 2.0

        normalized = normalized.clamp(0.0, 1.0)
        bin_indices = (normalized * (self.n_bins - 1)).long()
        return bin_indices + self.action_token_begin_id

    def decode(self, token_ids: Tensor) -> Tensor:
        """Decode action token IDs back to continuous values.

        Args:
            token_ids: (..., action_dim) token IDs.
        Returns:
            (..., action_dim) continuous actions.
        """
        bin_indices = (token_ids - self.action_token_begin_id).clamp(0, self.n_bins - 1)
        normalized = bin_indices.float() / (self.n_bins - 1)

        if self.min_action is not None and self.max_action is not None:
            lo = self.min_action.to(normalized.device)
            hi = self.max_action.to(normalized.device)
            return normalized * (hi - lo) + lo
        return normalized * 2.0 - 1.0

# VLA 模型全面调研报告

**调研日期**: 2026-05-20
**目的**: 寻找不同 connector 架构的开源 VLA 模型，扩展 vision connector 对 token 可压缩性影响的实验

---

| 模型 | Connector | 压缩行为 |
|------|-----------|----------|
| SmolVLA | Pixel-shuffle | Cliff-edge collapse (k=0.95 → 0% SR) |
| OpenVLA | 2-layer MLP projector | Graded degradation (线性下降) |
| RoboFlamingo | Perceiver Resampler | 尝试失败（gripper loss 无法训练） |

---

## Connector 类型覆盖分析

### 已有数据的 Connector 类型
| Connector 类型 | 代表模型 | 压缩行为 |
|---------------|----------|----------|
| Pixel-shuffle | SmolVLA | Cliff-edge collapse |
| 2-layer MLP projector | OpenVLA (Prismatic) | Graded degradation |
| Perceiver Resampler | RoboFlamingo | 训练失败 |

### 可新增的 Connector 类型
| Connector 类型 | 候选模型 | 特点 | 可行性 |
|---------------|----------|------|--------|
| **Linear projection** | **π0**, X-VLA, SpatialVLA | 最简单的 connector，单层线性变换 | ⭐⭐⭐ 高 |
| **Cross-attention (Flamingo-style)** | **RoboMM** | 不在 encoder 端压缩，而是 decoder 端通过 cross-attention 选择性融合 | ⭐⭐ 中 |
| **CNN patch → direct concat** | Octo | 无独立 connector，图像 patches 直接拼入 transformer | ⭐ 低（架构差异太大） |
| **MLP merger + spatial grouping** | LingBot-VLA | 先空间合并再 MLP 投射 + cross-attention | ⭐⭐ 中 |
| **Cross-attention tokenizer** | HPT | learnable tokens 通过 cross-attention 聚合 vision features | ⭐ 低（非 VLM 架构） |

### 关键发现
1. **Linear projection** 是最有价值的新增类型——π0 和 X-VLA 都用这种最简单的 connector，与 OpenVLA 的 2-layer MLP 形成对比
2. **Cross-attention** (RoboMM 的 OpenFlamingo 架构) 从根本上不同：不投射拼接，而是 decoder 层间交叉注意力
3. 大量模型共享 connector：OpenVLA, CogACT, LLARVA, TraceVLA, ECoT, OpenVLA-OFT 都用 **2-layer MLP**（Prismatic 或 LLaVA 架构）

---

## Top 推荐：最适合扩展实验的 5 个模型

### 🥇 1. π0 (Physical Intelligence)
- **Connector**: Linear projection (单层线性)
- **推荐理由**: 
  - 与 OpenVLA 的 2-layer MLP 形成直接对比（linear vs MLP）
  - 开源权重 + 代码，社区活跃
  - 已有 LIBERO 评测代码
  - PaliGemma 架构广为人知
  - 3B 参数可在单卡运行
- **预期价值**: Linear projection 不增加非线性变换，token 可能保留更多原始 visual feature 结构 → 压缩行为可能与 MLP 不同

### 🥈 2. X-VLA
- **Connector**: Linear projection + soft prompts
- **推荐理由**:
  - 同样是 linear projection，与 π0 对比看 soft prompt 的影响
  - LIBERO 98% SR，已有训练好的 LIBERO 权重直接可用
  - 0.9B 参数，实验成本最低
  - ICLR 2026，最新模型
  - Apache-2.0 开源
- **预期价值**: 验证 linear projection 的压缩行为是否 consistent across models

### 🥉 3. DeeR-VLA
- **Connector**: Perceiver Resampler + Cross-attention (OpenFlamingo)
- **推荐理由**:
  - Perceiver Resampler 与 RoboFlamingo 相同架构，但 DeeR-VLA 已验证可训练（CALVIN benchmark 正常工作）
  - 给 Perceiver Resampler 第二次机会
  - 可对比 RoboFlamingo 的训练失败是架构问题还是实现问题
  - Open source with checkpoints
- **预期价值**: Perceiver Resampler 本身就做了 attention-based compression → 压缩行为可能与 MLP/linear 截然不同
- **风险**: LIBERO 需要自己改造

### 4. RoboMM
- **Connector**: Cross-attention (OpenFlamingo) + 3D Adapter
- **推荐理由**:
  - Cross-attention 融合方式从根本上不同于 projection-based connectors
  - 已有 LIBERO 结果 (90.7%)
  - Open source
- **预期价值**: Cross-attention 在 decoder 端动态选择 visual features → 可能展现出与 projection-based 完全不同的压缩模式
- **风险**: 架构较复杂，3D adapter 增加变量

### 5. OpenVLA-OFT
- **Connector**: 2-layer MLP projector (与 OpenVLA 相同)
- **推荐理由**:
  - Connector 与 OpenVLA 相同，但 action generation 完全不同（continuous + chunking）
  - LIBERO 97.1% SOTA
  - 可验证 "相同 connector + 不同 action head" 是否影响压缩行为
  - 已有完整 LIBERO 代码
- **预期价值**: 作为 OpenVLA 的对照组，隔离 connector vs action head 对压缩的影响

---

## 不推荐的模型及原因

| 模型 | 排除原因 |
|------|----------|
| RT-2-X | 闭源，权重不可用 |
| GR-2 | 未开源 |
| 3D-VLA | 3D 点云输入，与 2D VLA 差异太大 |
| CogACT | Connector 与 OpenVLA 相同（Prismatic MLP），不新增类型 |
| LLARVA | Connector 与 OpenVLA 类似（MLP projector），不新增类型 |
| TraceVLA | Connector 与 OpenVLA 相同，不新增类型 |
| ECoT | Connector 与 OpenVLA 相同，不新增类型 |
| HPT | 非 VLM 架构，不适合 connector 压缩叙事 |
| GR-1 | 有 Perceiver Resampler（有价值），但无 LIBERO 支持 + 视频生成架构改造成本高 |
| Octo | 无独立 connector（CNN patch 直接拼入），架构与标准 VLM 差异太大 |

---

## 总结：Connector 类型 × 模型矩阵

| Connector 类型 | 已有 | 推荐新增 |
|---------------|------|----------|
| Pixel-shuffle | SmolVLA ✅ | — |
| 2-layer MLP projector | OpenVLA ✅ | OpenVLA-OFT（同 connector 不同 action head） |
| Perceiver Resampler | RoboFlamingo ❌(失败) | **DeeR-VLA** |
| **Linear projection** | — | **π0, X-VLA** |
| **Cross-attention** | — | **RoboMM** |

实现后可达 **5 种 connector 类型 × 6+ 模型**的全面对比。

---

## X-VLA 详细架构调研（2026-05-20 新增）

### 模型身份确认
- **名称**: X-VLA (Soft-Prompted Transformer as Scalable Cross-Embodiment Vision-Language-Action Model)
- **论文**: arXiv:2510.10274, ICLR 2026
- **GitHub**: [2toinf/X-VLA](https://github.com/2toinf/X-VLA)
- **HuggingFace**: [2toINF/X-VLA](https://huggingface.co/collections/2toINF/x-vla)
- **参数量**: 0.9B
- **许可**: Apache-2.0
- **LIBERO SR**: 98.1%

### 架构详解

```
Image (224×224) → Florence-Large (DaViT) → Vision Tokens [B, N, 2048]
    → Linear Projection + LayerNorm → [B, N, 1024]
    → Merge with Text Token Embeddings → Florence2 Encoder (self-attention)
    → Context Features → SoftPromptedTransformer (24 layers, hidden=1024)
        + Soft Prompts (32 learnable embeddings per embodiment)
        + Noised Action Tokens (flow matching)
    → Denoised Action Trajectory [B, 30, 20]
```

**各组件详情**:

| 组件 | 规格 |
|------|------|
| Vision Encoder | Florence-Large (DaViT): patch_stride=[4,2,2,2] → total stride 32 |
| Vision Token 数量 | ~49 tokens (7×7 at 224×224) 或 ~576 tokens (24×24 at 768×768) — **需实际加载模型验证** |
| Projection | Linear + LayerNorm, dim 2048 → 1024 (projection_dim=1024) |
| Soft Prompts | 32 tokens/embodiment, 0.04% of total params |
| Transformer | 24 layers, hidden=1024, 16 heads, mlp_ratio=4.0 |
| Action Head | Flow matching, 30 anchor points × 20 dims (EE6D), 10 denoising steps |
| Max Sequence | 512 tokens |

### HuggingFace 权重
| Checkpoint | 用途 | 地址 |
|------------|------|------|
| X-VLA-Pt | 预训练基座 (cross-embodiment) | 2toINF/X-VLA-Pt |
| X-VLA-Libero | LIBERO 全参数微调 (98.1% SR) | 2toINF/X-VLA-Libero |
| X-VLA-libero-*-peft | LIBERO LoRA 微调 (各 suite) | 2toINF/X-VLA-libero-spatial-peft 等 |

### 环境依赖
```
transformers<=4.51.3, torch, einops==0.8.1, timm==1.0.12, 
accelerate==1.2.1, peft==0.17.1, safetensors==0.4.5,
numpy==1.26.3, scipy==1.15.0, mmengine==0.10.5,
fastapi, uvicorn==0.34.3, h5py==3.12.1, pyarrow==20.0.0,
av==15.0.0, mediapy==1.2.4
```
LIBERO 评估另需 Python 3.8 环境。

### VTC 集成方案
**插入点**: Florence2 `_encode_image()` 输出 → **VTC** → `_merge_input_ids_with_image_features()`

**改造清单**:
1. 创建 `xvla_vtc_adapter.py`（复用 VisionTokenCompressor，hidden_dim 改 1024）
2. 创建 XVLASmartCompressWrapper，hook Florence2 vision 输出
3. 修改 merge 逻辑以适应压缩后的 token 数量
4. 创建 `train_xvla_smart_compress.py`（参考 X-VLA 的 train.py + peft_train.py）
5. 适配 flow matching loss（不同于 OpenVLA 的 cross-entropy）

**与 OpenVLA VTC 的关键差异**:
| 维度 | OpenVLA | X-VLA |
|------|---------|-------|
| hidden_dim | 4096 | 1024 |
| 原始 vision tokens | 256 | ~49-576 (待验证) |
| Action 范式 | Autoregressive (256-bin CE) | Flow matching (MSE+BCE) |
| Connector | 2-layer MLP | Linear + LayerNorm |
| 模型大小 | 7B | 0.9B |

**预计工作量**: 8-12 小时
- 代码改造: 4-6h（adapter + training script）
- 环境搭建 + 模型下载: 2-3h
- 验证 + 调试: 2-3h

## X-VLA 调研结论

**模型确认**: X-VLA（[2toinf/X-VLA](https://github.com/2toinf/X-VLA)），0.9B 参数，ICLR 2026，LIBERO 98.1% SR。

**架构**:
- Vision encoder: Florence-Large (DaViT)
- Connector: **Linear projection** (dim 2048→1024) + LayerNorm
- Backbone: 24-layer Transformer (hidden=1024, 16 heads)
- Action: Flow matching, 30 anchor points × 20 dims (EE6D)
- 特色: 每个 embodiment 有 32 个 learnable soft prompts

**Vision Token 数量**: DaViT total stride=32，224×224 输入下 7×7=49 tokens。但 Florence-2-Large 默认分辨率是 768×768 (24×24=576 tokens)，**需要加载模型后验证 X-VLA 实际使用的分辨率**。

**VTC 集成方案**: 插入在 Florence2 `_encode_image()` 输出和 `_merge_input_ids_with_image_features()` 之间，复用 VisionTokenCompressor（hidden_dim 改 1024）。需适配 flow matching loss。

**权重**: 使用 `2toINF/X-VLA-Libero` 作为起点（已在 LIBERO 上 fine-tune 到 98.1%）。

**预计工作量**: 8-12 小时（adapter 代码 4-6h + 环境 2-3h + 调试 2-3h）。

**与 OpenVLA 对比的关键点**: X-VLA 的 linear projection 不引入非线性变换，vision token 经过的变换远少于 OpenVLA 的 2-layer MLP。预期压缩行为与 MLP connector 存在质性差异——这正是论文需要的 "最简 connector" 数据点。

## X-VLA 调研结论

**模型确认**: X-VLA（[2toinf/X-VLA](https://github.com/2toinf/X-VLA)），0.9B 参数，ICLR 2026，LIBERO 98.1% SR。

**架构**:
- Vision encoder: Florence-Large (DaViT)
- Connector: **Linear projection** (dim 2048→1024) + LayerNorm
- Backbone: 24-layer Transformer (hidden=1024, 16 heads)
- Action: Flow matching, 30 anchor points × 20 dims (EE6D)
- 特色: 每个 embodiment 有 32 个 learnable soft prompts

**Vision Token 数量**: DaViT total stride=32，224×224 输入下 7×7=49 tokens。但 Florence-2-Large 默认分辨率是 768×768 (24×24=576 tokens)，**需要加载模型后验证 X-VLA 实际使用的分辨率**。

**VTC 集成方案**: 插入在 Florence2 `_encode_image()` 输出和 `_merge_input_ids_with_image_features()` 之间，复用 VisionTokenCompressor（hidden_dim 改 1024）。需适配 flow matching loss。

**权重**: 使用 `2toINF/X-VLA-Libero` 作为起点（已在 LIBERO 上 fine-tune 到 98.1%）。

**预计工作量**: 8-12 小时（adapter 代码 4-6h + 环境 2-3h + 调试 2-3h）。

**与 OpenVLA 对比的关键点**: X-VLA 的 linear projection 不引入非线性变换，vision token 经过的变换远少于 OpenVLA 的 2-layer MLP。预期压缩行为与 MLP connector 存在质性差异——这正是论文需要的 "最简 connector" 数据点。
